tweets.text:
this sucks, but is amazing

Friend's team at BigCo has run a shadow no-sprints / no-points / measure bets / start together approach at BigCo for 8mos in complete secrecy while following "the rules". Jira looked A+ :)

Presented outcomes today. Left the crowd speechless. YES.

Will always remember a developer’s feedback after being invited to a string of customer interviews:

“Interesting! For some reason I thought you just asked them what they want, and that’s what you came back to us with. But it is nothing like that. Please invite me next time.”

THIS IS THE RIGHT WAY

Vs.

This is how we do it. We’re optimizing for X, and navigating these trade offs. Here’s more about our context. We tried ___, but it opted for X because ___. A sign we might be on the right track might be ___.

Twitter encourages the former.

On a call

Product manager communicates flawlessly ... humble, crisp, coherent

I ask questions...

“I set aside 30m every Friday morning, revisit and update a mind-maps and my notes, and practice. Mostly practice. That 30m is easily the highest leverage thing I do each week.”
This obsession with keeping developers in delivery mode, topped up, cranking it out. Does the world really end if a team does discovery together(B) ?

Old fashioned, I guess, but I think a 12 month roadmap, continuously updated, is a reasonable ask.

The trick, however, is that beyond 1-3 months out, it is fully opportunity based and gracefully acknowledges and represents areas of uncertainty, assumptions, beliefs, etc.

Totally unscientific ....

But yeah, the % of time talking about "things" that aren't all that important in the grand scheme. And glossing over specific practices.

product managers have to communicate constantly...up/down/across the org

so they are practicing constantly.

which is why you need to give other folks time to form their thoughts/questions/push-back/ideas.

otherwise, the product manager will take the air out of the room

"We have 1600 items in the backlog. At 4.5 items/w that is 6.8 years. What should we do?"

Prioritize 54 (12 weeks). Export the rest into a text file. Done.
